summary: Bound review corrections to frozen witnesses and keep gate evidence in the canonical environment.
trigger: A long REVIEW accumulated new phrasing cases, and DONE-required evidence was first produced with a temporary timeout environment override.
lesson: When a reviewer proposes a language case outside frozen acceptance, classify it and create a traceable follow-up draft instead of expanding the current Story. Run done_required_validate without PROOF_OR_STOP timeout overrides because effectiveEnvironmentDigest is evidence-bound; rely on the CLI-derived command budget.
reusePrompt: Before expanding a review-language fix or adding timeout variables to an evidence command, retrieve the B-9a49 bounded-review and canonical-environment lesson.

summary: A documentation assertion built on a substring check survives deletion of the very sentence it claims to verify; assert the sentence and re-run against a corpus with it removed, requiring failure.
trigger: Writing or reviewing a case that checks documentation content, or any assertion of the form text.includes(SOME_NAME); also when an intent sentence names several clauses but the pinned case tests one.
lesson: Three separate findings in one story came from the same shape. A check for a command name passed even when the explanation around it was deleted, because the name appeared elsewhere in prose. A case-insensitive search for a bound phrase survived deleting the rule sentence, because a pre-mortem row repeated the phrase with different punctuation. Build documentation checks as a corpus of quoted sentences, assert each is present, then re-run the whole check against a copy with that one sentence removed and require the check to fail. Confirm each quoted sentence occurs exactly once in the document it is asserted against, or the mutation proves nothing.
reusePrompt: documentation check includes / grep survives deletion / tautological assertion / deletion mutation corpus / intent clause untested

summary: Narrowing a guard by disqualifying a term pair on proximity alone reopens the hole it protects; disqualify only when no decisive relation joins the two terms.
trigger: A guard false-positives on ordinary prose and the quick fix is to stop pairing two specific terms, or to remove a term from a detection list.
lesson: A guard paired a severity subject with a responsibility outcome within a character span, and ordinary prose about story priority tripped it. Disqualifying that one cell cleared the false positive but also admitted Priority alone decides the story, which is exactly what the guard exists to catch; a reviewer proved it by driving the real entry point rather than reading the diff. The correct shape is to disqualify the generic cell only when no decisive relation sits between the terms, reusing the verb vocabulary the file already has for its other detectors rather than inventing a second list. Any such fix needs true-positive fixtures in the same commit, one per axis, or the next reviewer cannot tell a narrowing from a disabling.
reusePrompt: guard false positive / disqualify term pair / severity authority / widened acceptance / true positive fixture

summary: A framework guard reading a story checklist can block every reviewer lane at review_run_start, and the checklist context is frozen outside INIT, so the fix belongs in the guard rather than the prose.
trigger: review_run_start fails identically for every lane with a task-context authority refusal naming a checklist field, and no lane has a review run recorded.
lesson: The whole REVIEW phase stops, not one lane, and there is no override on review_run_start. Reopening the story to INIT to reword the text resets non-pending checklist items to pending, so it costs more than fixing the guard. Treat it as acceptance-blocking for the current story and fix the guard in place with a scope acknowledgement, keeping true-positive fixtures. Reviewers that cannot obtain a run id will still do the work and report unsigned; read those reports, but re-run the lanes with signed runs afterwards, because unsigned findings are not gate evidence.
reusePrompt: review_run_start unsafe Finding-triage authority / every lane blocked / checklist context frozen / unsigned reviewer findings

summary: A guard that has never been observed failing is not evidence, and three guards in one story passed on exactly the defect they were written to catch.
trigger: Writing or reviewing a verification script, smoke guard, or contract check that is meant to prove a property.
lesson: Every guard needs a negative control BEFORE it is trusted: inject the exact defect it targets and confirm it fails. In B-3e16 three separate guards passed on their own target defect. verify-docs searched a whole 1400-line file so a deleted flag still matched elsewhere. verify-no-project-writes allowlisted by FILE, so a project-root write in an allowed file passed while printing a reassuring cache-derived reason. verify-clean-tree used the default warm cache, so no index rebuild fired and it measured nothing at all. Each produced specific, confident output. Also beware the control being broken rather than the guard: an `if (false && ...)` neuter can fail to compile and leave a STALE dist that reports PASS, and prefixing a condition into a compound `A || B` disables only A. A neuter must DELETE the check, and you must confirm the build succeeded and the dist actually changed.
reusePrompt: About to trust a verification script, smoke guard, or contract check? Search this before relying on it: negative control, guard passes on its own target defect, stale dist, vacuous guard.

summary: Fixing the demonstrated instance instead of the class produces a guard that is defeated again by the next spelling of the same attack.
trigger: Responding to a reviewer finding about a bypass, especially in a security or provenance check.
lesson: B-3e16 needed five versions of one write guard because each fix closed the instance shown rather than the class. The reviewer named it exactly: the class was never "single-letter alias", it was "the guard trusts the identifier name". Renaming the variable moved the instance and left the trust intact. A lexical rule cannot decide provenance, and worse, it inverted the incentive: it rejected an honestly named cache write while rewarding the rename that defeats it. The fix that held was measuring the EFFECT (run a real scan in a subprocess, hash every path, assert the repository is byte-identical), because that is primitive-agnostic and catches worker threads, child processes and sqlite alike. When a reviewer says a fix is instance-shaped, stop patching and ask what property is actually being asserted.
reusePrompt: Reviewer says a bypass is fixed but the same attack works through a different spelling? Search: instance versus class, lexical rule cannot decide provenance, measure the effect not the call.

summary: The cannotAutoSign rule is load-bearing: an independent host found twelve real defects that eleven in-session reviewer passes had approved.
trigger: Hitting review_assurance_floor, cannotAutoSign, or a host-verdict requirement and being tempted to treat it as bureaucratic friction.
lesson: In B-3e16 four reviewer lanes and a topology critic passed the story across three inventory waves. An independent host (codex, then claude via CLI) then found twelve real defects across twelve rounds, including live arbitrary code execution via an unvalidated --root, a security guard that could be defeated by a nested same-name producer, and a guard PRINTING coverage it did not have. Six of those defects were in guards written to close the previous finding. Note also that review_host_availability_probe reported all three hosts as execution_failure:timeout when codex actually worked fine when invoked directly - do not conclude no host is available from a probe timeout alone. Verdicts bind to materialHash, so a fix invalidates the pass that preceded it; re-earn it rather than submitting a verdict bound to code the host never saw.
reusePrompt: Blocked by cannotAutoSign, review escalation quorum, or a host verdict requirement? Search: independent host found what in-session lanes missed, probe timeout is not host unavailability, verdicts bind to materialHash.

summary: CLI next-step hints still print the retired "lattice dispatch" bin name, and a stale global lattice binary makes it fail plausibly instead of loudly.
trigger: Running reviewer_list, review_inventory or a REVIEW transition and reading the "Next:" line it prints.
lesson: B-a4e3 removed the dispatch aliases and CLAUDE.md mandates "proof-or-stop dispatch", but reviewer-list.ts:241, review-inventory.ts:239/251 and transition-effects.ts:254 still emit "Next: lattice dispatch ...". There is no bin/lattice in this repo, yet /opt/homebrew/bin/lattice resolves to a separate @lattice/core install reporting 0.3.257 while the repo builds 0.3.269. So copy-pasting the hint does not give command-not-found: it silently drives a twelve-version-stale binary against a different install, the same version-skew class .githooks/pre-push exists to prevent. The lattice-residue brand-prose gate misses it because its scan roots cover docs and markdown, not emitted runtime strings under packages/main/src. Any fix must also update the assert.match pins in review-inventory-epoch-smoke.ts:218/385 and lattice-parallel-wave-smoke.ts:338, which pin the old spelling. Note gap_log could not record this: it fails with invalid_binding_shape because B-META findings.json is a flat array with no provenance chain.
reusePrompt: Search dev-memory for "lattice dispatch" or "brand-prose runtime strings" before touching reviewer_list / review-inventory / transition-effects next-step output, or when extending verify-lattice-residue scan roots.

summary: A reviewer "cannot find the cited artifact" claim is often a search-scope error, not missing evidence -- verify before acting on it.
trigger: A REVIEW lane reports that evidence cited in a signed record does not correspond to any real artifact.
lesson: In B-3e16 the quality lane passed but flagged that assertLoaderArgumentProvenance and its "14 permanent mutants", cited in a signed review_escalation_fallback record, could not be found. It searched packages/graph and packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts. The guard actually lives in packages/main/src/tasks/retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts:5162, is invoked at :5653, and its mutant array holds exactly 14 tuple-form entries, each asserted to (a) really differ from the original, (b) keep the pinned argument byte-identical, (c) change the AST fingerprint, and (d) still trip the provenance pin when scanned with the MUTANT OWN fingerprint -- so re-pinning cannot launder a mutant. The evidence was accurate; only the search scope was wrong. Note the mutants use tuple form ["label", code], so a regex for /label:/ finds zero and looks like confirmation of the reviewer claim. Confirm with grep -rln across the whole package before filing a finding against signed evidence.
reusePrompt: Search dev-memory for "search-scope error" or "cited artifact not found" before filing a finding that signed evidence references a nonexistent artifact.

summary: effectiveEnvironmentDigest hashes the whole ambient environment minus a deny-list, so per-invocation host/terminal/OTEL variables make a DONE-required receipt unverifiable from any other shell.
trigger: done_prepare or lifecycle_check reports effective-environment-digest-mismatch[N] even though done_required_validate just returned PASS
lesson: The digest is recomputed at read time from the reader's own environment and compared to the value stored in done-required-evidence.json, so ANY ambient value that differs between the writing process and the verifying process breaks it. VALIDATION_TRANSPORT_ENV_KEY_LIST is digest-pinned by VALIDATION_TRANSPORT_ENV_KEYS_DIGEST and must stay byte-stable, so new keys are stripped at the filter seam in effectiveValidationCommandEnvironment (see HOST_LAUNCHER_SESSION_ENV_KEYS) rather than appended to the pinned list. But the leak has a long tail from independent sources: Claude Code (CLAUDE_PID, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET/TOKEN), cmux (CMUX_TERMINAL_LIFECYCLE_ID, CMUX_TAB_ID, CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID, CMUX_PORT*), Alacritty (ALACRITTY_LOG/SOCKET, PID-embedded), tmux (TMUX, PID-embedded), macOS (LaunchInstanceID), and OTEL (TRACEPARENT, whose span-id regenerates per invocation and therefore defeats any deny-list). Do not chase these one at a time: each fix costs a full lane re-earn plus a ~5 minute DONE-required suite. Instead launch BOTH the receipt writer and every later verifier from one identically-stripped environment via an env -u wrapper script; the digest then matches because both sides see the same environment. Verify stability first by running buildDoneRequiredExecutionIdentity twice through the wrapper and comparing effectiveEnvironmentDigest. The architectural fix (allow-list of semantically relevant vars such as PATH/NODE_OPTIONS/CI/locale instead of a deny-list) belongs in its own story.
reusePrompt: Search for effective-environment-digest-mismatch, TRACEPARENT, or done-required receipt unverifiable across shells before adding another key to HOST_LAUNCHER_SESSION_ENV_KEYS.

summary: A DONE-required receipt written by a separate process can never satisfy the DONE gate: writing it auto-commits story metadata, which moves HEAD and invalidates the receipt just written. Only done_prepare, which writes and consumes in one process, converges.
trigger: done_required_validate reports PASS with refusalReasons=none, but lifecycle_check --target=DONE still reports [BLOCKED] done.done-required-validation with effective-environment-digest-mismatch[0],[1]
lesson: Do not chase the digest by hand. The receipt IS valid at the instant it is written (a read inside that same run showed blockers: 0), but done_required_validate auto-commits done-required-evidence.json plus process-events, which moves headHash/materialHash, so the next separate reader recomputes a different identity and rejects it. Any write-then-read cycle across process boundaries therefore oscillates and never converges. The remedy is proof-or-stop done_prepare --mergeMain --refreshStale --validate, which is designed to write AND consume the evidence inside a single process, so the receipt is evaluated before its own metadata commit moves the hashes. This is also why the gate's own next: hint points at done_prepare rather than at re-running done_required_validate. Wasted effort to avoid: I first blamed PROOF_OR_STOP_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS (removed it, still mismatched), then AI_AGENT/SECURITYSESSIONID (stripped on both sides, still mismatched), then suspected reader non-determinism (false: my node -e probes each carried a different _ last-arg value, which is itself in VALIDATION_TRANSPORT_ENV_KEY_LIST, so the instrumentation perturbed its own input). A brute-force sweep removing each of ~79 env keys produced no match because the cause was never a single key.
reusePrompt: done_required_validate PASS but DONE gate still blocked on effective-environment-digest-mismatch? Search: done_prepare single-process write-and-consume, receipt self-invalidation via auto-commit.

summary: The CertificationWindow needs a FINALIZED UNCONSUMED review-inventory receipt, but story_advance --phase=DEV consumes it. Spend receipts on DEV remediation and the window becomes unreachable, since review_inventory_begin is REVIEW-only.
trigger: certification_window_begin fails [pre_cert_inventory_not_finalized] 'No FINALIZED unconsumed Review Inventory receipt is present', and done_required_validate then fails [pre_cert_window_required]
lesson: done_required_validate is an official heavy certification invocation, so whenever doneRequiredCommands is configured it unconditionally calls refuseHeavyCertificationUnlessAdmitted and needs an ADMITTED/RUNNING window. Do NOT conclude from isOfficialHeavyValidateInvocation (which gates only validate --full) that done_required_validate is exempt; it is not. certification_window_begin needs finalizedUnconsumedReviewInventory: state FINALIZED AND no consumedAt on either the epoch or the receipt. The trap is that story_advance --phase=DEV is the remediation path that CONSUMES the receipt, and review_inventory_begin is REVIEW-only, so if you spend every epoch receipt returning to DEV you arrive in TEST with none left and the window is unreachable without another full REVIEW cycle. On B-5a88 receipts RI-091, RI-092 and RI-094 were all consumed that way before the pattern was spotted. Correct order when a story needs both a DEV repair and a certification window: land all repairs in DEV, advance to REVIEW, run the epoch (lanes + critic), review_inventory_finalize, then advance REVIEW->TEST DIRECTLY (that transition does not consume), leaving the receipt available for certification_window_begin in TEST. Ignore the tool's own 'Next: story_advance --phase=DEV' hint at that point, and verify consumedAt is null on both epoch and receipt before advancing.
reusePrompt: certification_window_begin says pre_cert_inventory_not_finalized, or done_required_validate says pre_cert_window_required? Search: finalized unconsumed inventory receipt, REVIEW to TEST does not consume.

summary: Monkeypatching child_process functions with a bare wrapper silently breaks util.promisify(execFile) in every traced descendant because the wrapper drops the util.promisify.custom symbol.
trigger: A test or script that passes standalone fails only under done_required_validate / traced validate with TypeError reading .split or .stdout of undefined, or promisify(execFile) resolves a bare string instead of {stdout, stderr}.
lesson: The runtime tracer (validation-runtime-tracer.cjs) wraps spawn/exec/execFile/fork so traced runs observe process boundaries. exec and execFile carry an own util.promisify.custom symbol property that makes promisify resolve {stdout, stderr}; a plain wrapper function does not inherit own properties, so promisify falls back to the generic form resolving the first callback value (the stdout string), and destructuring {stdout} from a string yields undefined. The fix must copy own property descriptors onto the wrapper AND re-define promisify.custom with a tracing shim, because a plain descriptor copy lets promisified spawns escape the trace entirely. Regression coverage: validation-runtime-tracer-transparency-smoke.ts with a git-show negative control against the pre-fix tracer. General rule: any wrapper that replaces a Node builtin function must preserve its own symbols/properties (promisify.custom, Symbol.toStringTag) or downstream metaprogramming silently degrades only in the instrumented environment - the defect class is invisible to code review and to any test lane that does not run traced.
reusePrompt: traced test fails but passes standalone / promisify execFile resolves string / tracer wrapper transparency / TypeError split undefined under done_required_validate

summary: Registering a new test task requires THREE fail-closed membership authorities, not two; missing the third aborts the entire root suite rather than skipping that task.
trigger: Adding any new test:<name> task, or seeing `npm test` exit 1 within about a second with `canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[...]`.
lesson: This repo maintains THREE separately-maintained test-membership lists, and none is derived from another: (1) validate.commands in lattice.config.json, (2) the test:<name> script plus its entry in test:serial-reference in root package.json, and (3) RESOURCE_POLICY in packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts. The third is the one people miss and the most punishing to omit: entriesFromSerialReference fails CLOSED, throwing `canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[...]` at module load, so a serial-reference member with no RESOURCE_POLICY entry takes down `npm test` for the WHOLE repository instead of merely going unrun. Because npm test is a doneRequiredCommands entry, that also blocks done_required_validate and therefore DONE. Use the plain repoRead(name) policy for a task that only reads the repo and spawns the CLI against temp dirs; the name string must match the npm script and task filename exactly. This has now bitten at least four stories (B-cdf6, B-49ed, and B-9f2c twice over, since the decision doc that was supposed to prevent it itself said TWO). Verify with `node -e` calling entriesFromSerialReference directly and asserting unknownPolicy=[] rather than trusting a grep of two files.
reusePrompt: Adding a new test task, or npm test dies in under a second with canonical inventory mismatch / unknownPolicy? Search: three membership authorities, RESOURCE_POLICY fails closed, full-suite-runner.

summary: Signed artifacts auto-commit, so earning them one at a time never converges: batch every mutation first, freeze the tree, then earn all verdicts in one pass.
trigger: Chasing repeated stale_* / review_evidence_invalid / Prompt Envelope invalid blockers where fixing one artifact re-stales another.
lesson: Reviewer passes, verification receipts, delivery checks, rollout reports and scope acknowledgements all bind to the file set AND all auto-commit their own metadata. So any artifact earned before a later mutation is invalidated by that mutation, and earning them serially is a non-convergent loop. The fix is ordering, not retrying: FIRST enumerate every remaining blocker in one read (lifecycle_check --target=DONE lists them all), THEN perform every mutation (phase bounces, code and doc fixes, scope_contract_acknowledge, rollout regeneration, evidence refresh), THEN commit so the tree is frozen, and ONLY THEN earn the signed artifacts — dispatching all reviewer lanes simultaneously against that one commit so their envelopes share a changedFilesDigest. Corollary: reviewer lanes must be earned LAST among signed artifacts, because every other mutation invalidates them. In B-9f2c a doc fix that landed after two lanes had signed invalidated both and cost a full round; batching finished the same work in one. Also give each concurrently dispatched agent a UNIQUE scratchpad filename — two lanes told to use the same payload path overwrote each other mid-flight.
reusePrompt: Stuck in a loop where fixing one gate artifact stales another (stale_delivery_check, invalid_review_run_binding, Prompt Envelope invalid)? Search: batch mutations then freeze then earn, reviewer lanes last.

summary: Acknowledge out-of-scope paths before the first acceptance seal, not when the REVIEW gate asks
trigger: A story commits a fix touching a file outside its signed scope contract
lesson: scope_contract_acknowledge moves the scope-contract digest, which invalidates an already-sealed acceptance-basis (AT_SCOPE_BINDING_MISSING) and pre-review-check (PR_ARTIFACT_TAMPERED). The requirement only surfaces at story_advance REVIEW, so if you seal first you pay the full basis to rollout to live-proof to pre-review rebuild twice. Run scope_contract_check right after any out-of-scope commit and ack immediately. The CLI arg is --paths (JSON array), not --path.
reusePrompt: Before sealing acceptance artifacts, search dev memory for 'scope ack before seal'

summary: verification_evidence_refresh_stale rebinds hashes but never re-runs the pinned command
trigger: Coverage reads covered=0 after a refresh that printed Refreshed N/N stale evidence items
lesson: Refreshed N/N means REBOUND, not RE-EARNED. Every touched receipt becomes mechanical:false with nonMechanicalReason saying the pinned command was not re-run, and coverageStatusForCoveredEvidence then demotes executable intents to non_mechanical, so covered drops to 0 while every row still says result:pass. To genuinely re-earn, build verification_evidence_batch_add from each intent's own verificationIntent.LANE[i].verification {command,selector} plus its existing kind: one execution fans out to all rows. Two traps: a named intent stores its id as the FULL ref (CHK-001:edge:oversized-output-probe) so a positional loop invents a nonexistent edge:3 and is refused with intent_ref_unresolved -- derive refs from existing verificationEvidence[].intentRef; and preserve each row's original kind instead of overwriting all rows with one value.
reusePrompt: When coverage is 0 but all evidence says pass, search dev memory for 'refresh_stale rebinds not re-earns'

summary: Surface the review-assurance floor during REVIEW; on a single host only a human can clear it
trigger: A high-risk story reaches TEST with every mechanical gate green but doneClosure blocked
lesson: The DONE gate requires assurance three-round-two-hosts-or-degraded-single-host. On one machine autopilot_review_status reports independentHosts:0, so the 3x2 path is impossible -- and per-run lines may still read 'pass 2/2 passing hosts', which counts host ENTRIES not INDEPENDENT hosts, so never cite those as satisfying the floor. The only remaining path is review_escalation_fallback_set with eligibility single-host-environment, and cannotAutoSign explicitly bars done_prepare, story_advance and the story owner/main session from writing it. Run review_escalation_status while still in REVIEW so the human approval is requested before everything else is finished and idling.
reusePrompt: On a high-risk story in a single-host repo, search dev memory for 'assurance floor human only'

summary: A temporary filesystem mirror is not Git-isolated if its .git entry points to the real worktree administration.
trigger: Validation reports state_changed_before_launch despite unchanged HEAD and staged file contents while tests create linked repository mirrors.
lesson: Separate raw index bytes from staged-entry content and HEAD when diagnosing causal preflight drift. A mirror that links the real .git can allow ordinary Git commands to update the source index cache. Reproduce the structural shared-administration defect without writing the shared index; then use private admin/index/refs while sharing objects read-only as appropriate, and assert real index bytes, staged entries and HEAD remain unchanged across the complete harness. Preserve the production index guard. A passing standalone run does not identify the historical inner writer or prove that a task-scoped optional-lock setting repaired the defect.
reusePrompt: Search private Git mirror, raw index drift, unchanged staged contents, causal state_changed_before_launch.

summary: Distinguish causal refusal diagnostics from historical root-cause proof and confirm actual validation recovery.
trigger: A validation run aborts with a shared causal_preflight_refused surface error.
lesson: A shared refusal message does not establish whether owner-lease refresh, preflight signature verification or fact drift failed. Preserve the old log and its uncertainty. Add deterministic negative controls that prove each short-circuit branch and emit only safe reason codes or changed field names, never credential or fact values. Then retain the actual complete validation result separately: diagnostic GREEN does not itself prove operational recovery, and a later successful run does not retrospectively establish the old branch.
reusePrompt: Search B-fe8f causal preflight discriminating diagnostics versus historical attribution.
